es: Reconocer ofertas, contraofertas, rechazos y aceptaciones en una negociación cotidiana por un objeto de segunda mano.

teaching.en: My offer is eighty dollars for the bike.
teaching.es: Mi oferta son ochenta dólares por la bicicleta.
teaching.explanationEs: Offer: alguien propone una cifra o una condición. Con ella empieza la negociación.
segments: My offer is eighty
dollars for the bike.
teaching.audioText: My offer is eighty dollars for the bike.

teaching.en: That price is too high, so Mia made a counteroffer of sixty dollars.
teaching.es: Ese precio es demasiado alto, así que Mia hizo una contraoferta de sesenta dólares.
teaching.explanationEs: Counteroffer: respondes a una oferta con otra cifra o condición, sin rechazar de plano.
segments: That price is too high, so Mia
made a counteroffer of sixty dollars.
teaching.audioText: That price is too high, so Mia made a counteroffer of sixty dollars.

teaching.en: I'm afraid I have to refuse, but I could go a little lower.
teaching.es: Me temo que tengo que rechazar, pero podría bajar un poco.
teaching.explanationEs: Refuse + but: rechazas con tacto y dejas una puerta abierta. Lower significa más bajo.
segments: I'm afraid I have to refuse, but
I could go a little lower.
teaching.audioText: I'm afraid I have to refuse, but I could go a little lower.

teaching.en: Seventy is a reasonable price, so I accept.
teaching.es: Setenta es un precio razonable, así que acepto.
teaching.explanationEs: Accept cierra la negociación. Reasonable describe un precio que se considera justo.
segments: Seventy is a reasonable
price, so I accept.
teaching.audioText: Seventy is a reasonable price, so I accept.

teaching.en: OK, seventy dollars. It's a deal!
teaching.es: De acuerdo, setenta dólares. ¡Trato hecho!
teaching.explanationEs: It's a deal: el cierre habitual y amistoso. El sujeto it es obligatorio en inglés.
segments: OK, seventy dollars.
It's a deal!
teaching.audioText: OK, seventy dollars. It's a deal!

prompt.es: Mia responde con una contraoferta a Leo. ¿Qué mensaje escribe?

choices.text: It's a deal, ninety dollars!
Would you take seventy dollars?
I'm afraid I can't buy a bike.

feedback.es: Una contraoferta propone otra cifra: «Would you take seventy dollars?» cambia los noventa de Leo. Las otras dos aceptan o rechazan sin proponer nada.

hint.es: Busca el mensaje que propone una cifra distinta en forma de pregunta.

origin.text: Leo: The bike costs ninety dollars.

prompt.es: Mia está de acuerdo con la oferta de Leo. ¿Qué mensaje la acepta?

choices.text: Seventy-five is too high for me.
How about seventy dollars?
OK, seventy-five. You have a deal!

feedback.es: Aceptar es estar de acuerdo con la cifra y cerrar el trato. Las otras dos mantienen la negociación abierta: una rechaza y la otra propone otra cifra.

hint.es: Aceptar significa conservar la cifra y cerrar, no cambiarla.

origin.text: Leo: Seventy-five dollars, and it's yours.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Aceptarías sesenta dólares por la lámpara?»

feedback.es: La pregunta típica de la contraoferta es «Would you take + cifra?». También se entiende con accept.

hint.es: Es la pregunta típica de una contraoferta: Would you … + cifra.

feedback.es: Cada mensaje cumple una función: proponer una cifra, responder con otra, rechazar con tacto o cerrar el trato.

choices.text: She turns down the price and asks for more.
She makes her first offer.
She agrees and closes the deal.

choices.text: She refuses the price.
She makes a counteroffer.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estos mensajes es una aceptación?

choices.text: Sixty is too high for me.
OK, sixty. We have a deal!
My offer is sixty dollars.

feedback.es: «We have a deal» cierra la negociación. Las otras dos son un rechazo y una oferta.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me temo que tengo que rechazar tu oferta.»

feedback.es: Refuse (o turn down) es rechazar; el «I'm afraid» suaviza el rechazo.

origin.text: I'm afraid I have to ___ your offer.

answer.text: My offer is forty dollars for the lamp

feedback.es: La oferta empieza con My offer is + cifra + for + objeto.

title.en: On condition that, as long as
title.es: A condición de que, siempre que

es: Formular ofertas condicionales con provided that, on condition that y as long as, y conceder con although y even so.

teaching.en: We can book the hotel provided that the price includes breakfast.
teaching.es: Podemos reservar el hotel siempre que el precio incluya el desayuno.
teaching.explanationEs: Provided that + presente simple pone una condición. Después no se usa will.
segments: We can book the hotel provided
that the price includes breakfast.
teaching.audioText: We can book the hotel provided that the price includes breakfast.

teaching.en: I will pay half on condition that you buy the train tickets.
teaching.es: Pagaré la mitad a condición de que tú compres los billetes de tren.
teaching.explanationEs: On condition that: condición firme y más formal; se exige algo a cambio.
segments: I will pay half on condition
that you buy the train tickets.
teaching.audioText: I will pay half on condition that you buy the train tickets.

teaching.en: You can choose the hotel as long as it fits our budget.
teaching.es: Puedes elegir el hotel siempre que se ajuste a nuestro presupuesto.
teaching.explanationEs: As long as + presente simple: la condición más natural en conversación.
segments: You can choose the hotel as
long as it fits our budget.
teaching.audioText: You can choose the hotel as long as it fits our budget.

teaching.en: Although the hostel is far from the beach, it is cheap.
teaching.es: Aunque el hostal está lejos de la playa, es barato.
teaching.explanationEs: Although + oración reconoce un inconveniente (concesión). No se usa con but.
segments: Although the hostel is far from
the beach, it is cheap.
teaching.audioText: Although the hostel is far from the beach, it is cheap.

teaching.en: The train is expensive. Even so, we can afford it.
teaching.es: El tren es caro. Aun así, podemos permitírnoslo.
teaching.explanationEs: Even so une dos frases: la segunda sigue adelante pese a la primera. Lleva coma.
segments: The train is expensive. Even
so, we can afford it.
teaching.audioText: The train is expensive. Even so, we can afford it.

prompt.es: Sara solo irá si el hotel es barato. ¿Qué frase lo dice?

choices.text: I'll go although the hotel is cheap.
I'll go even so the hotel is cheap.
I'll go as long as the hotel is cheap.

feedback.es: As long as pone una condición: Sara irá solo si el hotel es barato. Although y even so expresan contraste, no condición.

hint.es: Busca el conector que pone una condición para el futuro.

prompt.es: El hostal está lejos, pero es barato. ¿Qué frase dice eso?

choices.text: Although the hostel is far, it is cheap.
Provided that the hostel is far, it is cheap.
As long as the hostel is far, it is cheap.

feedback.es: Aquí no hay condición, hay un inconveniente que se reconoce: eso es una concesión con although. Las otras dos ponen una condición absurda.

hint.es: No hay una condición: se reconoce un inconveniente y se sigue adelante.

prompt.es: Completa: «El vuelo es caro. Aun así, podemos permitírnoslo.»

feedback.es: Even so une dos frases separadas y se escribe con coma detrás.

hint.es: Son dos frases separadas: el conector va al principio de la segunda, con coma.

feedback.es: On condition that va seguido de presente simple: the price is fair, sin will.

feedback.es: La primera frase reconoce un inconveniente entre dos frases (even so); la segunda pone una condición (as long as, provided that u on condition that).

choices.text: Only when the ride costs more than thirty dollars.
When the ride costs thirty dollars or less.
At any price, because they are in a hurry.

feedback.es: As long as pone el límite del precio: el taxi es posible si no cuesta más de treinta dólares.

prompt.es: Ana quiere reservar el hotel aunque es caro. ¿Qué frase hace bien la concesión?

choices.text: Although it is expensive, but I will book it.
Even so it is expensive, I will book it.
Although it is expensive, I will book it.

feedback.es: Although + oración va sin but y con coma antes de la idea principal. Añadir but es un calco del español y even so no se une con una coma a la misma oración.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me apunto siempre que el viaje cueste menos de trescientos dólares.»

feedback.es: Para poner el límite de una condición se usa as long as (o provided that) con presente simple.

origin.text: I'll come ___ the trip costs less than three hundred dollars.

answer.text: I'll pay for the tickets as long as you pay for lunch.
accepted: I'll pay for the tickets as long as you pay for lunch.
I will pay for the tickets provided that you pay for lunch.
I'll pay for the tickets on condition that you pay for lunch.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase expresa bien una condición para el futuro?

choices.text: We will go provided that it is sunny.
We will go provided that it will be sunny.
We will go provided that it would be sunny.

feedback.es: Tras provided that va presente simple: it is sunny. Will y would después del conector son errores típicos del español.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aunque la habitación es pequeña, nos gusta.»

es: Identificar la postura, el límite y el compromiso final de dos personas que negocian oralmente el uso de un espacio.

teaching.en: Ana's position is clear: she needs the spare room on weekday evenings.
teaching.es: La postura de Ana es clara: necesita la habitación libre por las tardes entre semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Position: lo que alguien quiere conseguir. En el audio suele aparecer con need, want o I'd like.
segments: Ana's position is clear: she needs
the spare room on weekday evenings.
teaching.audioText: Ana's position is clear: she needs the spare room on weekday evenings.

teaching.en: Leo's limit is Saturday: he will not give it up.
teaching.es: El límite de Leo es el sábado: no va a renunciar a él.
teaching.explanationEs: Limit: lo que no acepta. Se oye con can't, won't o not after…
segments: Leo's limit is Saturday: he
will not give it up.
teaching.audioText: Leo's limit is Saturday: he will not give it up.

teaching.en: Leo insists on keeping Saturday, but he is flexible about Sunday.
teaching.es: Leo insiste en quedarse con el sábado, pero es flexible con el domingo.
teaching.explanationEs: Insists on + -ing marca una postura firme; flexible indica que hay margen para negociar.
segments: Leo insists on keeping Saturday, but
he is flexible about Sunday.
teaching.audioText: Leo insists on keeping Saturday, but he is flexible about Sunday.

teaching.en: In return, Leo accepts a limit: he will stop playing at eight.
teaching.es: A cambio, Leo acepta un límite: dejará de tocar a las ocho.
teaching.explanationEs: In return: lo que uno ofrece a cambio de que el otro ceda.
segments: In return, Leo accepts a limit:
he will stop playing at eight.
teaching.audioText: In return, Leo accepts a limit: he will stop playing at eight.

teaching.en: They reach a compromise: Ana takes the weekdays and Sunday, and Leo keeps Saturday.
teaching.es: Llegan a un compromiso: Ana se queda con los días laborables y el domingo, y Leo conserva el sábado.
teaching.explanationEs: Reach a compromise: llegar a un punto medio que aceptan los dos.
segments: They reach a compromise: Ana takes the
weekdays and Sunday, and Leo keeps Saturday.
teaching.audioText: They reach a compromise: Ana takes the weekdays and Sunday, and Leo keeps Saturday.

prompt.es: Escucha a Tom y elige cuál es su postura.

choices.text: He wants the living room for a night with friends.
He wants to study in the living room alone.
He wants the living room on Sunday morning.

feedback.es: La postura es lo que Tom quiere conseguir: la sala el sábado por la noche para recibir a sus amigos.

hint.es: La postura aparece después de I want o I need.

origin.audio: I want the living room on Saturday night. My friends are coming over.

prompt.es: Escucha a Mia y elige cuál es su límite.

choices.text: Tom cannot use the room at all.
The room must be free by midnight.
Mia wants the room all night.

feedback.es: Mia permite usar la sala, pero «not after midnight» es su límite: a medianoche debe quedar libre.

hint.es: El límite suele oírse con won't, can't o not after.

origin.audio: You can have the room, but not after midnight. I won't change that.

prompt.es: Completa: «Amigos hasta medianoche, pero sin música: es un buen compromiso para los dos.»

feedback.es: Un compromiso es la solución intermedia que acepta cada parte.

hint.es: Es la solución intermedia que aceptan los dos.

origin.text: Friends until midnight but no music: that is a good ___ for both of us.

prompt.es: Escucha a Sara y elige por qué no puede el viernes.

choices.text: She is travelling that day.
She has a test that day.
She has to work that day.

feedback.es: Sara da la razón de su límite con «because I work»: trabaja el viernes.

origin.audio: I can't do Friday because I work. How about Sunday afternoon instead?

pairs: I need the car on Friday.

feedback.es: Need expresa la postura, can't el límite, how about una propuesta y in return lo que se ofrece a cambio.

answer.text: That is my limit and I will not change it

prompt.es: Escucha el cierre del acuerdo sobre la bici y elige en qué quedan.

The speaker keeps Sunday and the other person uses Saturday.
They both use the bike on Sunday.

feedback.es: Tom pide el garaje el viernes; Sara no puede y ofrece el sábado como alternativa.

choices.text: Ana uses the printer on Tuesday morning.
Leo uses the printer on Monday before noon.
Leo uses the printer on Tuesday morning.

answer.text: They reached a compromise and everyone was happy

feedback.es: Reach a compromise es el verbo natural para llegar a un punto medio.

es: Rechazar con tacto una oferta de reparto de gastos y responder con una contraoferta, una condición y una concesión.

teaching.en: Thank you for your offer, but I'm afraid I can't accept it.
teaching.es: Gracias por tu oferta, pero me temo que no puedo aceptarla.
teaching.explanationEs: I'm afraid: rechazo con tacto. Antes se agradece y después se usa but.
segments: Thank you for your offer, but
I'm afraid I can't accept it.
teaching.audioText: Thank you for your offer, but I'm afraid I can't accept it.

teaching.en: I suggest that we split the bills sixty-forty.
teaching.es: Sugiero que repartamos las facturas en un sesenta y un cuarenta.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest that + sujeto + verbo: es la contraoferta. Split significa repartir; bills, facturas.
segments: I suggest that we
split the bills sixty-forty.
teaching.audioText: I suggest that we split the bills sixty-forty.

teaching.en: Would sixty-forty be fair, since I am away on Saturdays?
teaching.es: ¿Sería justo un sesenta-cuarenta, ya que estoy fuera los sábados?
teaching.explanationEs: Fair + una razón con since: justificas tu contraoferta sin atacar la del otro.
segments: Would sixty-forty be fair, since
I am away on Saturdays?
teaching.audioText: Would sixty-forty be fair, since I am away on Saturdays?

teaching.en: I'd rather split the internet bill equally.
teaching.es: Preferiría repartir la factura de internet a partes iguales.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd rather + verbo base expresa preferencia sin sonar brusco.
segments: I'd rather split the
internet bill equally.
teaching.audioText: I'd rather split the internet bill equally.

teaching.en: Instead of paying half, I'm willing to cook on Sundays.
teaching.es: En lugar de pagar la mitad, estoy dispuesto a cocinar los domingos.
teaching.explanationEs: Willing to + verbo es una concesión explícita. Instead of + -ing presenta la alternativa.
segments: Instead of paying half, I'm
willing to cook on Sundays.
teaching.audioText: Instead of paying half, I'm willing to cook on Sundays.

prompt.es: Rechaza con tacto la oferta de tu compañero. ¿Qué frase usas?

choices.text: No, I don't want that.
Thank you, but I'm afraid I can't accept that.
That is a bad idea, sorry.

feedback.es: Un rechazo con tacto agradece primero y luego usa but con I'm afraid. Las otras dos son secas o critican la idea.

hint.es: Un rechazo con tacto empieza agradeciendo y después usa but.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sugiero que repartamos las facturas de otra manera.»

feedback.es: Suggest that + sujeto + verbo es la forma natural de hacer una contraoferta.

hint.es: Es el verbo para proponer una alternativa y va seguido de that.

origin.text: I ___ that we split the bills in a different way.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Preferiría repartir el gasto a partes iguales.»

prompt.es: Escribe tu respuesta a la oferta de reparto de gastos, de 75 a 150 palabras.

answer.text: Hi Mia, thank you for your offer, but I'm afraid I can't accept it. I am away on Saturdays, so paying half of the bills would not be fair for me. Instead, I suggest that we split them sixty-forty, and I would pay forty percent. Although I use the kitchen less than you, I'm willing to cook on Sundays, as long as you do the dishes afterwards. I'd rather find a fair solution than argue about money. Would that work for you? If you agree, we can write it down and start this month.
accepted: Hi Mia, thank you for your offer, but I'm afraid I can't accept it. I am away on Saturdays, so paying half of the bills would not be fair for me. Instead, I suggest that we split them sixty-forty, and I would pay forty percent. Although I use the kitchen less than you, I'm willing to cook on Sundays, as long as you do the dishes afterwards. I'd rather find a fair solution than argue about money. Would that work for you? If you agree, we can write it down and start this month.

Dear Mia, thanks for asking, but I'm afraid I can't agree to fifty-fifty. I am not at home on Saturdays, so I do not use the kitchen or the living room very much. Instead, I suggest that we split the bills sixty-forty, and I would pay forty percent. I'm also willing to cook on Sundays, provided that you wash the dishes afterwards. I think that is a fair plan for both of us. Would that be OK with you? Let me know, and we can start next month.

feedback.es: La respuesta completa rechaza con tacto, propone sesenta-cuarenta, concede cocinar los domingos y pone una condición (as long as) sobre los platos.

origin.text: Datos: tu compañera Mia propone pagar las facturas al cincuenta por ciento. Tú estás fuera los sábados. Rechaza con tacto, propón un sesenta-cuarenta (tú pagas el cuarenta), ofrece cocinar los domingos como concesión y pon una condición: que ella lave los platos después.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase concede algo de forma explícita?

choices.text: I'm afraid I can't pay more.
I'm willing to pay a little more.
I suggest that you pay more.

feedback.es: Willing to + verbo es una concesión: aceptas hacer algo. Rechazar («I'm afraid…») y pedir que pague el otro («I suggest that you…») son otros movimientos de la negociación.

prompt.es: Completa: «Prefiero esperar antes que discutir.»

feedback.es: I'd rather + verbo base + than + verbo base compara dos opciones y expresa preferencia.

origin.text: I'd ___ wait than argue.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Gracias por preguntar, pero me temo que no es posible.»

answer.text: Thanks for asking but I'm afraid that is not possible

feedback.es: El agradecimiento va primero; el but con I'm afraid suaviza el rechazo.

es: Negociar un plan compartido de compañeros de piso: intercambiar ofertas, ceder dos veces y registrar el acuerdo final con sus condiciones.

prompt.es: Carlos hace una oferta con condición. ¿Qué frase lo hace?

choices.text: I'll pay the internet although you buy the food.
I'll pay the internet even so you buy the food.
I'll pay the internet provided that you buy the food.

feedback.es: Provided that + presente simple pone la condición de la oferta. Although y even so expresan contraste, no condición.

hint.es: Una oferta con condición exige algo a cambio: busca el conector de condición.

prompt.es: Completa: «Carlos hace una segunda concesión y acepta lavar los platos.»

feedback.es: Hacer una concesión es ceder algo a propósito; en inglés, make a concession.

hint.es: Es lo que haces cuando cedes algo para acercarte al otro.

prompt.es: En el chat de internet, ¿qué mensaje es la contraoferta de Carlos?

choices.text: Twenty-eight. It's a deal!
Would you take twenty-five?
I suggest we pay thirty each.

feedback.es: Carlos rechaza los treinta de Sara y propone veinticinco con «Would you take twenty-five?». Veintiocho es el cierre y treinta la oferta de Sara.

origin.text: Sara: The internet costs sixty dollars. I suggest we pay thirty each. Carlos: I'm afraid I can't pay thirty. Would you take twenty-five? Sara: Twenty-five is too low. Let's say twenty-eight. Carlos: Twenty-eight. It's a deal!

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué condición pone la hablante para ir a la fiesta.

choices.text: The other person must pay for the party.
The speaker refuses to come.
The other person must choose the music.

feedback.es: As long as introduce la condición: ella irá si el otro elige la música. Although solo reconoce que no le gustan las fiestas.

origin.audio: Although I don't like parties, I'll come as long as you choose the music.

prompt.es: Completa el registro del acuerdo con la primera oferta de Tom y la condición final.

feedback.es: Tom empieza ofreciendo pagar el gas y al final pone como condición que Sara haga la compra.

sentences: Tom's first offer: he pays the ___.
The final condition: Sara must do the ___.
origin.text: Tom: I'll pay the gas provided that you pay the electricity. Sara: I can't. How about half each? Tom: Fine, as long as you do the shopping.

prompt.es: Escribe como Sara el acuerdo final con Tom: dos concesiones y una condición.

answer.text: Hi Tom, here is our final agreement. Our total budget is five hundred dollars a month. You first offered to pay the rent, provided that I paid the bills, but I suggested three hundred and two hundred because that is fair. In the end, we settled on that plan. I made a concession: I will also pay for the internet. You gave in on the cooking: you will cook on weekdays, as long as I clean the flat on Sundays. So we agree that the rent is three hundred and the bills are two hundred. Is that OK with you?
accepted: Hi Tom, here is our final agreement. Our total budget is five hundred dollars a month. You first offered to pay the rent, provided that I paid the bills, but I suggested three hundred and two hundred because that is fair. In the end, we settled on that plan. I made a concession: I will also pay for the internet. You gave in on the cooking: you will cook on weekdays, as long as I clean the flat on Sundays. So we agree that the rent is three hundred and the bills are two hundred. Is that OK with you?

Hi Tom, this is our agreement. The total budget is five hundred dollars a month. First you offered to pay the rent on condition that I paid the bills, but I'm afraid that was not fair, so I suggested three hundred and two hundred instead. As a concession, I am willing to pay for the internet too. You are ready to give in on the cooking, provided that I clean the flat on Sundays. In the end, we settled on this plan and we are both happy. So we agree that the rent is three hundred and the bills are two hundred. Is that fine with you?

feedback.es: El registro incluye el total, la oferta con condición, dos concesiones, el resumen y la confirmación final.

origin.text: Datos: presupuesto total de 500 dólares al mes. Tom ofreció pagar el alquiler si Sara pagaba las facturas; Sara contraofertó 300 y 200. Concesión de Sara: pagará también internet. Concesión de Tom: cocinará entre semana, siempre que Sara limpie los domingos. Cierra confirmando el acuerdo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase registra bien un acuerdo final?

choices.text: So we agree that Mia pays the internet and Carlos cooks on Sundays.
So we agree that Mia pays the internet and Carlos cook on Sundays.
So we agree that Mia pays the internet provided that Carlos will cook on Sundays.

feedback.es: Para registrar el acuerdo se usa So we agree that + verbos en presente con su -s de tercera persona. Hay que evitar cook sin -s y will después de provided that.

prompt.es: Completa: «A veces hay que ceder para cerrar el trato.»

feedback.es: Give in significa ceder ante el otro, que a menudo es lo que hace falta para cerrar un trato.

origin.text: Sometimes you have to ___ in to close the deal.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Al final, llegaron a un acuerdo justo.»

answer.text: In the end they reached a fair agreement

feedback.es: In the end abre la frase para contar cómo terminó la negociación.
